To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
glutaminase was localized in mitochondria of the perikarya of a small subset of neurons within the neocortex.
the mitochondrial enzyme glutamine synthetase (GS) is immunocytochemi‐cally detectable within the presynaptic terminals of a subpopulation of neocortical and striatal neurons.

glutaminase‐immuno‐reactivity was detected in association with mitochondriain the somata of neurons and astrocytes of the cerebral cortex and caudateputamen nuclei, but was not detected in the presynaptic terminals of glutamatergetic neurons in either region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cellular and sub cellular localization of the mitochondrial enzyme glutamine‐ase (EC 2.6.1.1) in rat forebrain.
the role of the glutamatergicsynapse in the regulation of neuronal function, with a focus on the role of glutamate release from nerve terminals.
the development and application of immunocytochemical techniques for studying the cellular and sub-cellular distribution of glutamate and glutamine in the central nervous system.

glutaminase‐immuno reactivity is present throughout the cytoplasm of glutamate‐releas ing neurons and in mitochondria of all cells, but that glutaminase immunoreactivity is not present in glutamate‐receiving neurons.
, within the neocortex, glutaminase immunoreactivity is present in both perikaryal and synaptic sites.
glutaminase‐immuno‐reactivity is present in the mitochondria of glutamatergetic neurons and in the mitochondria in the terminals of glutamatergeic neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the enzyme is not enriched within glutamatergicsynapses, but rather occurs within the mitochondria of glutamatergie neurons and glia.
glutaminase occurs within mitochondria throughout the cytoplasm of many glutamate‐receiving cells.
glutaminase‐immuoreactivity is present in both the mitochondria and the cytoplasm in a variety of neurons and glial cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
glutaminase‐immuoreactive perikaryas are not confined to glutamatergiceurons.
glutaminase‐immnunoreactive terminals are not exclusively associated with asymmetric synapses, as has been previously suggested.
glutaminase‐immunoactivity is not restricted to glutamate‐contain‐ ing neurons and that the enzyme can occur within non‐mitochondri‐al cytoplasmic compartments in addition to mitochondria.
